prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Columbus. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Columbus Ohio for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do this precisely — but first: which “Columbus” do you mean (Columbus, OH; Columbus, GA; Columbus, IN; etc.) and do you have a ZIP code or insurance preference? Also tell me if you prefer a specialist (oral surgeon or periodontist) vs. a general dentist who places implants.

If you want an immediate, general answer (Columbus, OH), here’s a practical plan and what to call — including the types of offices you should contact and why — so you can quickly find a good implant provider.

Which specific practices to call (who to search for)
- Oral surgeons (maxillofacial surgeons) — call for surgical placement of implants, bone grafting, impacted-tooth extractions or complex anatomy. They handle the surgical portion and referrals to prosthodontists for crowns.
- Periodontists — specialists in the supporting tissues of the teeth who frequently place implants, especially when gum/bone health or grafting is needed.
- Prosthodontists or implant-focused restorative dentists — call when you want the final crown/bridge/denture and for complex restorative planning (aesthetic or full-mouth cases).
- Dental schools/teaching clinics — good option if cost is a concern; supervised specialists perform care.

Why call those specific types
- Experience with implants and complex cases reduces complication risk.
- Better access to CBCT 3D imaging, guided surgery, and advanced grafting.
- Coordinated surgical + restorative care for predictable results and warranty/aftercare.

How to find and vet specific practices near you
- Use these directories and filters: ADA Find-a-Dentist, American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) “Find an Implant Dentist,” American Academy of Periodontology, and Google Maps (look for many reviews and photos). Filter for “implant” or “periodontist” and read recent patient reviews.
- Look for credentials: board-certified or AAID/ICOI membership, fellowship in implant organizations, and training (postgraduate residency or fellowship).
- Confirm they use CBCT for planning, place modern implant systems (Nobel Biocare, Straumann, Astra, Zimmer, etc.), and offer a written treatment plan with a cost estimate and alternatives.

What to ask when you call (quick script)
1. Do you place dental implants in-house (surgery + restoration) or do you partner with another provider?  
2. How many implant cases do you place per month/year? How long have you been placing implants?  
3. Will I get a CBCT 3D scan and a written treatment plan?  
4. What implant system do you use and do you offer a warranty/guarantee on the implant?  
5. Do you do bone grafts/sinus lifts if needed? How do you handle sedation/anesthesia?  
6. What is the estimated total cost (surgery + implant + abutment + crown) and financing options?  
7. Do you have before/after photos and patient references for cases like mine?  
8. Is there a free or low-cost consultation to review options?

Typical cost/timeframe to set expectations
- Single implant (surgery + crown) commonly $3,000–$6,000 or more depending on grafting, location, and provider. Bone grafts/sinus lifts add cost/time.
- Treatment can take 3–9 months if grafting or healing is required; immediate implants are possible in some situations.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and list 5–8 specific implant practices (oral surgeons, periodontists, prosthodontists, and a dental school clinic) in your ZIP code or a specified Columbus (OH, GA, etc.), with short reasons to call each.
Tell me which Columbus and your ZIP or neighborhood, plus any insurance and budget preferences, and I’ll pull together a targeted list.
